main_text.p: expressum : sicut de Pallade, quæ Athenis. Legendum arbitror, Faria sive Pharia: quasi dixerit Cererem, quæ in Ægypto. Et intelligi credam Isidem : quæ nomine divertit à Cerere, numine communicat. CereriPharia siveÆgyptia
In Apuleio ¹, ipsa de se Isis: Me primigenii Phryges Pessinuntiam matrem nominant, me Eleusinii vetustam deam Cererem.
Eusebius de Præparatione ²: Φασὶ τοίνυν Αἰγύπτιοι τ̀ μὲν Ὀσίριν εἶναι τ̀ Διόνυσον, τὴν δὲ Ἴσιν τὴν Δήμη-τρα: Aiunt Ægyptii Osirim esse Bacchum, Isidem vero Cererem.
¹ Lib. xi. de Asin. ² Lib. ii. cap. i.

page.notes: Greek and Hebrew-like forms in the Eusebius and Herodotus passages are approximate; marginal notes "Cereri", "Pharia sive", "Ægyptia" are read from the right margin; the Herodotus Greek is uncertain. Lower part of page is faded with stains.
